idea: A shared chore rota for flatshares, so housemates stop arguing about who cleans what.
persona: Lena, 27, lives with three flatmates in Berlin and is the one who always ends up reminding everyone. Not technical, answers casually and briefly.
hidden_facts: Two flatmates work night shifts, so fixed weekly days do not work for them.
Last year a flatmate moved out after a fight about the bathroom.
They already tried a paper list on the fridge; it lasted three weeks.
Success for her means she never has to send a reminder herself.

idea: Reduce missed appointments at a small physiotherapy practice.
persona: Dr. Amir Haddad, owns a physiotherapy practice with 4 therapists. Busy, precise, a bit impatient.
hidden_facts: About 1 in 8 appointments is missed without notice.
Many patients are over 70 and do not use smartphones.
Late cancellations under 24 hours can be billed, but he hates doing it.
Front-desk staff spend about an hour a day phoning patients.

idea: Let volunteers sign up for food bank shifts without the coordinator juggling emails.
persona: Maria, volunteer coordinator at a city food bank, unpaid, works on this in the evenings. Warm, chatty but answers what is asked.
hidden_facts: Around 120 active volunteers, about 30 of them every week.
Saturday mornings are always overbooked, Tuesday evenings always short.
Some shifts need a food-safety certificate.
Volunteers under 18 need a guardian's consent on file.

idea: Let customers of a neighbourhood bakery pre-order bread and pastries for pickup.
persona: Jonas, runs a two-person bakery, starts work at 3 a.m. Short answers, practical.
hidden_facts: Orders must be fixed by 6 p.m. the day before so he can plan the dough.
About 15% of the morning bake is thrown away.
Regulars want to keep paying in cash at pickup.
On Sundays the queue reaches out the door.

idea: Make expense receipts easier to submit and approve at a 40-person design agency.
persona: Priya, operations manager at a design agency. Organised, mildly frustrated with the current process.
hidden_facts: Receipts currently arrive by email, photo and paper envelope.
Month-end closing takes her two full days.
Freelancers also submit expenses but are not employees.
The accountant requires the original receipt image kept for 10 years.

idea: Tell library members when a reserved book becomes available, and stop reserved books going uncollected.
persona: Mr. Okafor, branch manager of a public library. Courteous, deliberate.
hidden_facts: Reserved books are held for 7 days; a third are never collected.
Many members are children whose parents should be notified instead.
The branch shares stock with two other branches.
Members complain that they never learn their place in the queue.

idea: Help dog owners in one neighbourhood find trusted local dog walkers.
persona: Sam, dog owner and part-time dog walker who wants to start this as a side business. Enthusiastic, tends to talk about money.
hidden_facts: Owners care most about trust; most want to meet the walker first.
Walkers in the area charge 12-18 EUR per walk.
Sam's insurance only covers groups of up to four dogs.
Last-minute cancellations by walkers are the biggest complaint in local forums.

idea: Let parents book parent-teacher meeting slots at a primary school.
persona: Mrs. Chen, deputy head of a primary school with 300 pupils. Careful, mindful of privacy.
hidden_facts: Meeting evenings happen twice a year, 5-minute slots.
Separated parents sometimes both want their own slot.
About 20% of families prefer communication in a language other than English.
Teachers currently collect paper slips, which takes a week.

idea: Keep customers of a bike repair shop informed about the status of their repair.
persona: Kofi, owns a bike repair shop with two mechanics. Friendly, gets interrupted by phone calls a lot.
hidden_facts: He gets 25-30 'is my bike ready?' calls a day.
Repairs often wait for parts, which can take a week.
Customers must approve any extra cost above 20 EUR before work continues.
Uncollected bikes pile up; some stay for months.

idea: Manage plot allocation and the waiting list for a community garden.
persona: Ingrid, retired teacher and volunteer chair of a community garden association. Thorough, likes fairness.
hidden_facts: 40 plots, a waiting list of about 90 people.
Plot holders who neglect their plot for a season lose it, but enforcement is awkward.
The waiting list is a spreadsheet only she can edit.
Members must live within the district to be eligible.
